articles.title: UK GPs are most stressed and likely to quit profession, international survey reports
articles.author: Jacqui Wise
articles.summary: GPs in the UK reported the highest levels of work related stress compared with primary care doctors in nine other high income countries, an international survey has found.UK GPs were also the least satisfied with time spent per patient, daily workload, work-life balance, and income…

articles.title: NHS Grampian: Inquiry will be held over surgical deaths “cover-up”
articles.author: Bryan Christie
articles.summary: An inquiry is to be held into claims that the Scottish government covered up a report that found liver and pancreatic surgical deaths at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary were nine times the national average.The four year old report has been made public for the first time…

articles.title: Menopause hormone therapy med popularity increases 141% compared to previous years
articles.author: Theresa Gaffney and Annalisa Merelli
articles.summary: In June 2026, 4.9M menopause hormone therapy medications were dispensed to cisgender women in the U.S. between the ages of 40 and 74.

articles.title: A step towards modelling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in primates
articles.author: albert-c.ludolph@uni-ulm.de (Liubov Novikova)
articles.summary: A new primate model offers a promising first step towards reproducing the spread of ALS pathology across synapses, although important differences from the stereotyped patterns observed in human disease remain to be addressed.

articles.title: [Editorial] Multiple sclerosis: beyond controlling relapses
articles.author: The Lancet
articles.summary: Few neurological diseases have seen a transformation in diagnosis and treatment as remarkable as multiple sclerosis. A chronic, heterogeneous autoimmune condition, it typically begins in early adulthood and affects over 3 million people, with women roughly three times more likely to be affected than men.

articles.title: [Comment] Remibrutinib: a high-efficacy disease-modifying drug for relapsing multiple sclerosis?
articles.author: Gilles Edan, Emmanuelle Le Page
articles.summary: Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors directly modulate the functions of B lymphocytes and myeloid cells (notably macrophages and microglia) and thus target both the adaptive and innate mechanisms that contribute to the immunopathology of multiple sclerosis on either side of the blood–brain barrier.

articles.author: Monica M. Bertagnolli
articles.summary: New England Journal of Medicine, Volume 395, Issue 20, Page 2063-2067, November 19, 2026.

articles.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age
articles.summary: A major analysis of 149 studies found that cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non-users, with the difference growing to more than six years among adults 30 and older.

articles.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression.

articles.title: Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary: Depression in older adults may be more than a mental health concern. Scientists discovered that accumulating tau protein, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, was linked to worsening depressive symptoms in people who still had normal memory and thinking abilities.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
articles.author: FDA
articles.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved the first medicine for treating limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), a rare inherited muscle disease, for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.

articles.title: FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years
articles.author: FDA
articles.summary: The FDA today approved Wilserdly (giredestrant), used alone after surgery in adults with estrogen receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer — the most common subtype of the disease.

articles.title: DiaMedica shares signs that drug extends pregnancy in fetal growth restriction trial
articles.author: Nick Paul Taylor
articles.summary: DiaMedica Therapeutics has shared phase 2 results in severe early-onset fetal growth restriction, reporting that most participants with known delivery dates remained pregnant longer than expected.

articles.title: Why Iambic’s CEO believes preclinical cancer therapy could be ‘holy grail’ for CDK inhibitors
articles.author: Marissa Russo
articles.summary: Fresh off a $150 million IPO, Iambic Therapeutics has unveiled preclinical data for a potential challenger in one of oncology's most competitive drug classes: cyclin-dependent kinases.

articles.title: Tiny iron particles boost light-based therapy to eliminate hidden tumors
articles.summary: Some cancer cells slip past even the most precise treatments and then grow back. Researchers at Nagoya University in Japan may have found a way to reach them. The team improved a light-based cancer treatment by adding tiny iron particles.

articles.title: PEPPER trial compares aspirin and anticoagulants after joint replacement
articles.summary: A large, multi-site clinical trial involving researchers at the University of Maryland School of Medicine (UMSOM) has provided important new evidence about the medications commonly used to prevent potentially life-threatening blood clots following hip and knee replacement surgery.

articles.title: Insurance coverage lags behind advances in maternal-fetal surgery
articles.summary: While maternal-fetal surgery has rapidly advanced to treat serious congenital conditions before birth, a new national study led By Penn Nursing reveals that insurance coverage policies and policy transparency have not kept pace.

articles.title: 'I'm amazed every day': Woman marks one year with a pig kidney
articles.summary: A New Hampshire woman has now lived for one year with a kidney from a gene-edited pig, the longest any patient is known to have done so.

articles.title: Uneven access to cancer surgeons is linked to higher digestive cancer mortality
articles.summary: Nearly half of U.S. counties have no surgeon who performs gastrointestinal or hepatopancreatobiliary (liver, pancreas, gallbladder and bile ducts) cancer operations, and residents of those counties have higher death rates from several of those cancers even after accounting for socioeconomic factors and rurality, according to…

articles.title: Custom MRI tool could show within weeks if pancreatic cancer treatment is working
articles.summary: About 60% of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer don't qualify for surgery because their disease is too advanced.

articles.title: Continuing advanced therapies before elective Crohn's surgery may reduce serious complications
articles.summary: Patients with Crohn's disease who continue advanced therapies, including biologics and small-molecule drugs, in the months before elective colorectal surgery may have a lower risk of two postoperative complications: anastomotic leak and organ space surgical site infection, according to a study published in the Journal…

articles.title: [Corrections] Correction to Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2026; 11: 1037–47
articles.summary: Yaqub S, Valberg M, Bjørnbeth BA, et al. Aspirin after curative-intent treatment of colorectal cancer liver metastases (ASAC): a multicentre, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

articles.title: Study reveals how zinc deficiency reshapes the gut microbiome
articles.summary: A new Cornell University study suggests that even a mild, chronic shortage of zinc can quietly rewire the intestinal tract, and that the small intestine and the colon respond in strikingly different ways.

articles.author: Benjamin H. Mullish

articles.title: Contemporary management of Crohn’s disease: optimizing outcomes
articles.author: Remo Panaccione
articles.summary: Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41575-026-01290-w Strategy studies published in 2026 demonstrated that, with already approved medications or established surgical approaches, better outcomes for patients with Crohn’s disease can be achieved.

articles.title: Multi-cancer detection tests for gastrointestinal cancers
articles.author: Chyke Doubeni
articles.summary: Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41575-026-01279-5 In this Perspective, Shaukat and colleagues describe the status and challenges of multi-cancer detection tests for a range of gastrointestinal cancers, including colorectal, liver, pancreatic and oesophageal cancers.

articles.title: CAF-macrophage crosstalk fuels immunotherapy resistance
articles.author: Liu, Y., Wang, L.
articles.summary: Gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis (GCPM) remains a formidable clinical challenge, characterised by poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Gut feeling: extracellular vesicles dictate livers susceptibility to colorectal cancer metastasis
articles.author: Fiori, M. E.
articles.summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global health issue, ranking as the third most common tumour and the second leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide.1 Distant metastasis is the primary cause of fatality for patients with cancer.

articles.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about Sanofi buying Insmed, Roche touting its breast cancer pill, and more
articles.author: Andrew Joseph
articles.summary: Sanofi is buying the biotech Insmed for $41 billion, the largest biopharma acquisition in years and one that will give the French firm two new approved drugs

articles.title: STAT+: Roche’s potential breast cancer blockbuster drug wins second FDA nod
articles.author: Elaine Chen and Andrew Joseph
articles.summary: Roche's breast cancer pill has picked up its second FDA clearance in a week, this time in early-stage breast cancer for use after surgery.

articles.title: Urgent Care’s Expanding Role in Identifying Mental Health Crises
articles.author: Dan Frogel
articles.summary: Tools like the ASQ and a growing range of care options can help providers catch mental distress signals and route patients to the right level of care.

articles.title: Data Quality in Practice: The One Question Worth Remembering
articles.author: Nathan Elliott
articles.summary: This simple four-word question is at the heart of everything we are doing with data quality.

New WHO technical package to help countries improve health data for COVID-19 response and beyond
articles.summary: Today, as part of its commitment to strengthening health information systems and improving health[1], especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, WHO announced a new approach to improving access to life-saving data: the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package.

articles.title: COVID-19 disrupting mental health services in most countries, WHO survey
articles.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted or halted critical mental health services in 93% of countries worldwide while the demand for mental health is increasing, according to a new WHO survey.

articles.title: Why government is slow — and how to fix it | Li Hongyi
articles.summary: Government is slow at solving problems — and technologist Li Hongyi wants to fix that. In a quick talk, he introduces his experimental team in the Singaporean government, which visits schools, hospitals, fire stations and communities with one goal: to find problems and prototype solutions.

articles.title: Weak and immature management putting patients at risk at failing health board, review finds
articles.summary: A review finds targets and money being prioritised over patient care at Betsi Cadwaladr health board.

articles.title: Nurses vote for industrial action over pay
articles.summary: Nurses will take continuous action short of strike from 3 December - such action includes working to rule and a ban on overtime.

articles.title: Was Benjamin Franklin the original wellness bro? I lived like him for a day to find out
articles.author: Madeleine Aggeler
articles.summary: Before online influencers existed, the founding father published an annual wellness pamphlet. I followed his 13 virtues he found necessary for a good life Benjamin Franklin doesn’t get enough credit.

articles.title: When Disaster Strikes, Medicaid Work Rules Add Barriers for Potential Enrollees
articles.author: Ashley Mizuo
articles.summary: Medicaid provides a critical safety net for people to maintain healthcare coverage. But new work requirements create barriers for those trying to recover from natural disasters.

articles.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
articles.author: Kate Wells
articles.summary: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

articles.title: As States Lose OB-GYNs, Some Look To Limit Medical Malpractice Risk
articles.author: Anika Nayak
articles.summary: Since 2025, at least four states have enacted laws restricting medical malpractice lawsuits. Patient advocates warn that the laws impose more of a burden on families harmed during childbirth and often pass with little attention.

articles.title: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
articles.author: Emmet Livingstone
articles.summary: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

articles.title: PNG’s parliament is voting on ratifying Bougainville independence. A ‘no’ won’t be the end of the story
articles.author: Tania Miletic, Co-Director, Initiative for Peacebuilding, Faculty of Arts, The University of Melbourne
articles.summary: After more than a century of colonial rule, a brutal war and a hard-won peace, Bougainville is approaching the finals steps of its road to self-determination.
